transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess what brings me in is… I’ve been having these evenings after work where I eat much more than I planned to. It’s not every single night, but especially on days when I’ve been really strict with myself all day, by the time I get home I’ll have dinner, and then it’s like I keep going—cereal, crackers, whatever leftovers are in the fridge, something sweet—just sort of one thing after another over a couple of hours.

And afterward I’m sitting there thinking, “Why did I do that? I wasn’t planning to eat all of that.” It feels embarrassing to even say out loud, because I’m 50 years old and I feel like I should have a handle on this, but it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should talk to someone instead of pretending it’s nothing.
How do you feel about yourself after these episodes of eating more than you planned?

Afterward I feel pretty bad about myself, honestly. Not just “oh, I ate too much,” but it turns into this whole judgment of myself, like I’ve let myself get out of control or I don’t look put together. And I know that might sound dramatic, but it really gets tied up with how I think I look, especially around work.

Like, if I’m getting dressed the next morning and my waistband feels tight before a client luncheon or one of our leadership meetings, I immediately start thinking I look sloppy. I’ll be standing there trying on pants or tugging at my blouse, and in my head I’m thinking, “They’re not going to take me seriously if I look like this.” Which is frustrating, because I know I still do my job. I know I can sit in a meeting and talk through policies and numbers and handle clients just fine. But in that moment it feels like my body is somehow making me look less professional, or less competent, and then I’m mad at myself for eating that way the night before.
Do you ever try to make up for these episodes of eating by doing something to counteract the calories, like exercising more or skipping meals the next day?

Yes… I do, though I don’t usually think of it in those exact words at the time. The next day after one of those nights, I’ll sort of make a plan in my head that I’m going to “get back on track,” but if I’m being honest, it’s more like I’m trying to make up for what I ate.

So I might skip breakfast and tell myself I’m just not hungry, and then lunch comes around and I’ll say, “Well, I already made it this far, I can just wait until dinner.” Or if I do eat something, I’ll try to keep it very small. It feels like I’m balancing the scales, I guess.

And sometimes I’ll push myself with exercise more than I probably should. Like I’ll take an extra-long hike, or if I’m doing softball conditioning, I’ll push harder even if I’m tired or my body is telling me I should ease up. I tell myself it’s discipline, but underneath it there’s definitely this feeling of, “You have to fix what you did last night.”
Do you ever make yourself vomit after one of these episodes of eating more than you planned?

I… I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I don’t really have a clear thing to point to there. It’s not something I’ve been thinking of as part of what’s happening, if that makes sense.

After those nights, I’m usually more in my head about what I ate and how bad I feel about it, and then I start thinking about what I’m going to do the next day. But making myself vomit specifically… I don’t know. That’s not the piece that stands out to me or what I’ve been coming in worried about.
Do you ever use laxatives or diuretics as a way to try to counteract the calories from one of these episodes of eating more than you planned?

I don’t think so… I mean, not in any kind of intentional way like that. I’ve never really thought, “I’m going to take something to get rid of what I ate,” if that’s what you mean.

I know what laxatives are, obviously, and I’ve heard people talk about water pills and things like that, but that’s not really part of what I do after those nights. My mind usually goes more to, like, “Okay, don’t eat so much tomorrow,” or trying to be stricter with myself. I don’t really have a routine of taking pills or anything like that to undo it.

I guess I’m hesitating because I’m trying to be careful and not give you the wrong answer. But no, I can’t think of using laxatives or diuretics for that reason.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yes… I think I am. I mean, I don’t walk around saying that out loud, and I try to tell myself I’m too old to be thinking this way, honestly. But it does get in my head.

Like, if I’m getting dressed for work and my waistband feels tight, especially before something where I have to be “on,” like a client luncheon or a leadership meeting, it can really throw me. I’ll start thinking I look sloppy or like I don’t look pulled together enough, and then I worry people won’t take me as seriously. And I know, logically, I’m still doing my job. I’ve been doing this a long time. My ability to talk to clients or handle accounts didn’t change because my pants feel tight that morning.

But in the moment it feels bigger than that. It’s like my brain connects it to whether I look professional, whether I look in control, whether people are judging me. So yes, I guess I am afraid of gaining weight, or at least afraid of what I think gaining weight would mean about me.
How often would you say these episodes of eating more than you planned happen in a typical week?

Most weeks, I’d say. It’s not every single night or anything like that, but over the past few months it’s been pretty regular… usually maybe one or two nights in a week where I end up eating way more than I meant to.

And then the next day I kind of go into damage-control mode, I guess. I’ll tell myself I should skip breakfast or lunch, or I’ll try to exercise longer than I normally would, like I have to make up for it somehow. It’s usually after one of those nights that I start making all these plans in my head about being stricter the next day.
Have you ever made yourself vomit after eating?

I… I don’t know how to answer that neatly. I don’t think of it as something I do in a planned way, like, “Okay, now I’m going to go make myself throw up.” That’s not really how it sits in my head.

There have been times after eating too much where I’ve felt so full and upset with myself that I’ve wanted the feeling to stop, and I’ve gone into the bathroom and sort of… tried to see if I could, I guess. But I don’t know if I’d say it’s a regular thing, or something I’m good at, or even something I always follow through with. I’m sorry, that probably sounds evasive. It’s just embarrassing to say out loud.

Mostly I feel ashamed afterward, and then I don’t want to think about it. So if you’re asking whether vomiting is my main way of dealing with it, I don’t think so. But have I ever tried? …yes, I think I have.
How often have you tried to make yourself vomit after eating more than you planned?

I’m not sure I can give you a clean number. It’s not something I’ve been tracking, and honestly I think part of me avoids thinking of it as a “thing” I do, if that makes sense.

It’s not every time I overeat. Not even close. Most of the time I just feel awful and sit with it, or I tell myself I’ll be stricter the next day. The vomiting part has been more like… a few times where I was really uncomfortable and upset and went into the bathroom and tried. But I couldn’t tell you, like, “once a week” or “twice a month” with any confidence.

If you’re asking recently, I’d say it’s been occasional, not regular. But I also feel embarrassed enough about it that I may be downplaying it a little without meaning to. I just know it hasn’t felt like my main pattern.
How many times have you made yourself vomit in the past month?

I honestly don’t know the exact number. I wish I could just give you one, because I know that’s what you’re asking, but I haven’t been keeping track, and it’s one of those things I try to push out of my mind afterward.

In the past month… I think it was only a small number of times, not something happening every few days. Maybe a couple? But even saying that makes me nervous because I’m not sure if I’m remembering accurately or if I’m sort of rounding it down because I’m embarrassed. It’s not like I have it written down anywhere, and when it happens I don’t exactly want to mark it on a calendar.

So I guess the most honest answer is: I’m not sure. I know it has happened, but I can’t give you a reliable count for the past month.
How many times in the past month have you had an episode where you ate much more than you planned?

That’s a little easier to answer than the vomiting question, but I still don’t have an exact count. In the past month… I’d say it’s happened on some evenings after work, not every night, but enough that it’s what made me feel like something was wrong.

It usually happens when I’ve been really strict with myself all day, like trying to keep everything under control, and then I get home and it’s like I lose the thread. I’ll mean to just have dinner, but then it turns into cereal, crackers, whatever leftovers are there, and then something sweet if we have it. And it’s all within a couple of hours, not spread out over the whole day.

If I had to estimate, maybe several times this month? I’m sorry, I know that’s vague. It’s not once or twice total, but it’s not every single day either. It’s more like certain evenings where I come home tired and hungry and then eat much more than I planned.
Have you made yourself vomit after eating more than you planned more than twice in the past month?

I’m… honestly not sure enough to say yes or no to “more than twice.” I know that probably sounds evasive, but I don’t want to give you a number just to make the question go away.

There were times after I ate more than I meant to where I felt panicky or ashamed and went to the bathroom and tried to make myself throw up. But whether that happened more than two times in the past month specifically… I can’t confidently say. It all kind of blurs together afterward, and I don’t exactly sit there thinking, “Okay, that was one,” because I mostly just want to forget it happened.

If I had to describe it, I’d say it’s been occasional, not like a regular routine every time I overeat. But I don’t trust myself enough to give you a clean yes or no on the “more than twice” part.
Do you usually try to make yourself vomit after these episodes of eating more than you planned?

I don’t know if I’d say “usually.” That word feels a little too definite, like it’s something I do every time or almost every time, and I’m not sure that’s true.

There are definitely times after I’ve eaten more than I planned where the thought comes up right away, like, “I need to undo this,” and I feel really panicky and ashamed. Sometimes I do try to make myself vomit. Other times I just sit with it and feel awful, or I tell myself I’m not going to do that this time. So it’s not automatic, exactly.

I guess the most honest way to put it is that I sometimes try, but I don’t think I can say I usually do. It depends on how upset I am afterward and how out of control the eating felt.
Have you made yourself vomit after eating more than you planned at least three times in the past month?

I’m sorry, I know you’re asking it more clearly, like “at least three times,” and I still don’t feel completely sure saying yes to that.

I can remember a couple of times where I definitely tried after eating too much, but when I try to count whether it was three or more in just this past month, I get stuck. It’s not something I’ve been tracking, and afterward I mostly feel embarrassed and try not to think about it. So I don’t want to say “yes, definitely three” if I can’t actually back that up.

I guess the most honest answer is: I’m not sure. It may have been, but I can’t confidently say it was at least three times.
Have you engaged in both binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors, such as self-induced vomiting, at least once a week for the past three months?

For the past few months, yes, it’s been happening most weeks, if I’m being honest. Not every single day or anything like that, but usually there’s one or two nights in a week where I eat way more than I planned to. And then afterward I feel like I have to make up for it somehow.

It’s not always vomiting. I know you mentioned that, and I’ve talked about that, but a lot of the time it’s more like the next day I’ll skip meals, or I’ll make myself exercise longer than I normally would because I feel like I need to balance it out. I’ll tell myself I’m just “being good” or “getting back on track,” but really it’s because I feel guilty about what I ate the night before.

So… yes, in that broader sense, the eating too much and then trying to compensate for it has been at least once a week for the last few months.
Have you made yourself vomit after eating more than you planned at least once a week for the past three months?

I don’t think I can say that clearly, no. I mean, I know there have been times I’ve made myself vomit after eating more than I meant to, but once a week for three months specifically… I’m not sure that’s accurate.

It’s hard because when you ask it that way, I start trying to go week by week in my head, and everything sort of blurs together. Some weeks it may have happened, and other weeks I don’t think it did. I tend to remember more the feeling afterward—the panic and disgust with myself—than the exact number of times or whether it was every single week.

So I guess my honest answer is: I’m not sure, and I don’t want to say yes to once a week for three months if I can’t really be certain.
How many times in the past three months have you had an episode where you ate much more than you planned?

I’m not sure I can give you an exact number, but it’s been… several times over the past three months. What brought me in is that some evenings after work, especially if I’ve been really strict with myself all day, I get home and I end up eating way more than I meant to.

It’ll start as dinner, and then I’ll think, okay, I’m still hungry, or I already messed up, and then it turns into cereal, crackers, leftovers, maybe something sweet, all within a couple of hours. It feels like much more than I planned when I started eating.

So I don’t have a clean count, like “this many times,” but those evenings have definitely been happening repeatedly over the last few months.
On average, how many times a month would you say you have an episode where you eat much more than you planned?

I’d say probably around four to six times a month, if I’m averaging it out. It’s hard to pin down exactly because I don’t always think of it as an “episode” at the time. It’ll just be one of those evenings after work where I’ve been really strict with myself all day, like barely eating or only eating what I think I’m “supposed” to, and then when I get home it sort of unravels.

I’ll have dinner, and then it doesn’t stop there. I’ll go back for cereal, then maybe crackers, leftovers, something sweet if there’s anything around, and before I know it a couple hours have gone by and I’ve eaten way more than I meant to. So if I’m being honest, it’s usually about once a week, sometimes twice in a bad week.
Have you made yourself vomit after eating more than you planned at least once in the past week?

I’m honestly not sure I can say yes to that. In the past week specifically… I’m trying to think back over the days, and I don’t want to answer too quickly just because I’ve done it at other times.

There was definitely at least one evening where I ate more than I meant to and felt really upset afterward, but whether I actually made myself vomit this past week after that—I don’t think so, but I’m not completely confident. The days kind of run together when I’m embarrassed about it, if that makes sense.

So I guess my best answer is: I don’t think I have in the past week, but I’m not totally sure.
Have you made yourself vomit after eating more than you planned in the past three months?

I’m… honestly not completely sure how to answer that. Over the past three months, there have definitely been times after eating too much where I felt awful about it, like really ashamed and panicky, and I remember thinking I wanted to undo it somehow.

But if you’re asking specifically whether I made myself vomit after those times, I don’t have a clear count in my head. It’s not something I’ve been tracking, and I think I kind of try not to think about it afterward. So I don’t want to say a definite yes or no if I’m not sure.

I guess what I can say is that it’s been on my mind after those episodes, and there may have been times, but I’m having trouble being exact about it.
